title: Othniel Delivers Israel and Judges (40 years)
summary: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, defeats Cushan-rishathaim; "the land had rest forty years" (Judg 3:9–11).
description: Judges-period record added from James B. Jordan's chronology (secondary display) with Ussher, Jones and, where available, CFAH-1 Table 1 dates for sorting. Jordan treats the judgeships as partly overlapping regional sequences (North / Centre / South) fitted to the 480 years of 1 Kgs 6:1 and the 300 years of Judg 11:26.

sorting_basis.note: Tier 3: Ussher-Jones (F. N. Jones): 1418 BC (no higher-tier year available). Jordan (secondary display) never sets the sort.

chronologies.date: OTHNIEL "40 YRS": 1418 BC (2586 AM) to 1378 BC (2626 AM); Cushan's 8 years (1418–1410 BC) fall inside the 40
chronologies.citation: Jones, Chart No. 4 "Judges to the First 3 Kings" (© 1993 Floyd Jones; chart text revised "As of 2007"), timeline band
chronologies.note: Jones counts the land's 40 years from the start of the oppression ("the periods of servitude must not be added to the time in which the land is said to enjoy rest but, rather, subtracted from it", 2002 ed. p. 91).

chronologies.date: 2599d AM, 1405 BC (Othniel defeats Cushan; land at rest 40 years)
chronologies.citation: Ussher, Annals of the World, Fourth Age §342 (paragraph numbering of the modern transcription)
Jordan, From Creation to Solomon (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2, Biblical Horizons, Oct. 2001), ch. 11 "The Era of the Judges and the Reign of Saul", p. 51
chronologies.note: 2001 revision. Jordan's 1991 list (BC 3:8) has an earlier year; see the second Jordan entry.

chronologies.date: "2602 - Defeat of Cushan, beginning of Othniel's 40-year judgeship (Jud. 3:11)."
chronologies.citation: Jordan, "Chronology and Kings (II)," Biblical Chronology 3:8 (August 1991), section "The Judges", summary list
chronologies.note: 1991 scheme, superseded by Jordan himself in 2001 (Studies in Biblical Chronology No. 2 dates the whole judges sequence 26 years later because he there ends the 300 years of Judg 11:26 when Ammon took the villages, AM 2860, not at Jephthah's victory).

chronologies.citation: Anno Mundi Chronology Studies (unnamed compiler; a compilation of James B. Jordan's system), p. 11, chart table "Biblical History According To A.M & B.C. Dates"
chronologies.note: Agrees with Jordan's own published AM 2628. The compilation's B.C. year (1382) is AM subtracted from 4010 (its own convention: Creation 4010 B.C.); Jordan's own SBC B.C. figures differ. Display only; never converted or used for sorting.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 6 "The Special People of God", PDF p. 192 (printed p. 191)
chronologies.note: Table of the judges ("Approximate Date"); the period of the judges is headed 1400-1095 BC (p. 191). Differs from the sort year (1418 BC, ussher-jones) by 18 years.
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "1418–1378 BC" (PDF p. 316): 18 years earlier (ranges overlap).

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 13 "The Special People of God–Taking the Promised Land", PDF p. 316 (printed p. 302)
chronologies.note: Table of the judges (pp. 316–317), which follows Ussher–Jones.

open_questions: Judges (1985), pp. 55–56: "Othniel probably died long before these forty years were up" - Jordan does not take the 40 years as the length of Othniel's life or office.
